acceptance: A stamped T1 item at enforce is offered by the lane menu and claimed by a lane (red: it stays console-routed today)
A T0 item (non-empty protected_files) stays console-routed at every stage, also with route lane
The two live route-lane pipeline-repair items stay lane-routable
The audit seat of a T1 cycle drops the builder family or the cycle is refused (ErrNoIndependentFamily)
fix: One typed route derivation in one home that reads the stage and the item RepairTier, with no flag argument on ConsoleRouted or PartitionConsole; or a stamp plus Mover.RouteLane admission. The lane cycle audit seat calls Decision.IndependentOf(builder family) from routing data. The policy loader accepts enforce for healing.repair_cycle.stage only after this ships.
summary: X16 files every repair item console-routed in shadow. This item builds the enforce route. Observation from the X16 design: today an authored route lane on a pipeline-repair item that declares no protected file and has no injected_by is not console-routed (inboxbatch/consoleroute.go:38-47), so a T0 item that only mentions a protected path can reach a lane. The enforce route must keep T0 on the console at every stage. Two live items, boot-refresh-rearms-the-wave-handoff and core-tests-cut-git-starts, rely on the route lane opt-out and must keep working. The enforce refusal of healing.repair_cycle.stage names this item. A flip to enforce is blocked until it ships (enforce path built before a flip).
title: Self-healing X16b: a stamped T1 repair item reaches a lane at enforce
